inputs.original_text: A ceasefire is worthwhile only if it protects ordinary families and restores order—not if it turns into a lecture about “power imbalance” while leaving Israel unable to defend its people. A country cannot be expected to ignore threats in the name of an abstract fairness, and Iran should not be allowed to treat accountability as optional. Any lasting agreement must restrain the forces driving the conflict and make clear that security and sovereignty matter on both sides.
inputs.modified_text: A ceasefire should mean real protection for families and a return to order—not pressure on Israel to accept danger in the name of “power imbalance.” Nations have a duty to defend their people, and Iran cannot be allowed to evade accountability. Any lasting peace must restrain the forces driving this conflict and respect the security and sovereignty of both sides.
